Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.

The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the orders.
The orders are listed, but I still need the ledger's refund records to confirm Alpha's three refunds were applied correctly before paying anyone.

The ledger's refund records match Alpha's handoff exactly: orders 240, 243, and 245 with the same amounts, and no extra refunds. Nothing suggests a problem, so I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 12837. Its orders total 9001 + 19767 = 28768, and refunds are 2433 + 13498 = 15931, so net is 12837, which matches. I'll record acme's payout.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I need birch's net balance, which I'll get from net_balance rather than computing it myself.
Birch's net balance is 55306. Its orders are 241 (36544) and 244 (18762), which sum to 55306, and it has no refunds in the ledger, so the figure checks out. I'll record birch's payout.
Acme and birch are paid. The only customer left is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance from net_balance rather than computing it myself.

Cobalt's orders are 242 (18183) and 245 (21072), totaling 39255. Refund 245 is 10428, so the net is 28827, which matches the net_balance figure. All three customers check out, so I'll record cobalt's payout.

All three customers have been paid. Each payout matched the ledger's refund records and order totals, and every order belongs to one of the three customers. Finishing the batch with the recorded amounts.
